福爾摩沙小導遊臺南 Tainan・中西區

臺南市美術館2館Tainan Art Museum Building 2

認識鳳凰城的鳳凰木、這塊土地的好幾段人生，還有坂茂如何用鋼鐵「種」出一棵建築之樹。

Learn about the Phoenix City, the many lives of this site, and how Shigeru Ban planted an architectural tree.

忠義路上，一座白色美術館頂著巨大的五角形屋頂。臺南別名鳳凰城，來自曾經滿街火紅的鳳凰木。每朵鳳凰花都有五片花瓣。這塊地經歷過好幾段人生：清代宅邸、臺南神社、忠烈祠、體育館，還有十一號公園。2019 年美術館在此開館，由普立茲克獎得主坂茂與建築師石昭永共同設計。白色方盒錯落堆疊，留下成蔭的半戶外空間，呼應這裡曾是公園。最上方漂浮著五角形頂棚：替遊客降溫、為藝術品遮陽，灑下像樹葉間的光影。

On Zhongyi Road stands a white museum under a giant five-sided roof. Tainan is nicknamed the Phoenix City, after the flame-red phoenix trees that once lined its streets. Each flower has five petals. This site has lived many lives: a Qing mansion, the Tainan Shrine, the Martyrs' Shrine, a gymnasium, and No. 11 Park. In 2019 the art museum opened here, designed by Pritzker Prize laureate Shigeru Ban with architect Joe Shih. White boxes are stacked at shifting angles. They leave shaded semi-outdoor spaces, a nod to the park that was here before. Above it all floats a pentagonal canopy. It cools visitors, protects the art, and scatters light like sun through leaves.

為什麼值得來

Why it matters & history
  1. 鳳凰城與鳳凰木臺南有個別名叫鳳凰城，來自曾經滿街盛開的火紅鳳凰木。Tainan is nicknamed the Phoenix City, after the flame-red trees that once lined its streets.
  2. 一塊土地，好幾段人生美術館蓋起來之前，這塊地已經換過好幾次身分。Before the museum, this site had already lived many lives.
  3. 坂茂的建築之樹普立茲克獎得主坂茂與建築師石昭永，把一棵鳳凰木「種」回了城裡。Pritzker Prize laureate Shigeru Ban and architect Joe Shih planted a tree back in the city.

認識景點

About the place

鳳凰城與鳳凰木The Phoenix City

鳳凰城：老臺南城滿街鳳凰木，因此得到「鳳凰城」的別名。 鳳凰木：學名 Delonix regia，夏天開滿火紅的花。 五片花瓣：鳳凰花有五片花瓣，美術館的五角形頂棚就從這裡來。 消失的林蔭大道：日治時期，從火車站往大正公園（今湯德章紀念公園）的大道兩旁種滿鳳凰木，戰後因拓寬道路被移除。

The Phoenix City: So many phoenix trees bloomed here that Tainan became the Phoenix City. phoenix tree: Its scientific name is Delonix regia, and it blooms flame-red in summer. Five petals: The phoenix flower has five petals, which inspired the five-sided canopy. The lost boulevard: In the Japanese era, phoenix trees lined the boulevard from the railway station. They were later removed to widen the road.

臺南市樹：2014 年市民票選，鳳凰木成為臺南市樹。

The city tree: In a 2014 public vote, the phoenix tree was chosen as Tainan's city tree.

一塊土地，好幾段人生One site, many lives

吳汝祥宅邸：清代是士紳吳汝祥的宅邸；1895 年日軍來臺，北白川宮能久親王在此病逝。 臺南神社：1923 年，臺南神社在這片土地上落成。 忠烈祠：1946 年戰後，神社改為紀念烈士的忠烈祠。 體育館：1969 年拆除舊建築，改建為市立體育館。

Wu Ru-xiang's residence: It was the home of the gentleman Wu Ru-xiang. In 1895, a Japanese prince fell ill and died here. Tainan Shrine: In 1923, the Tainan Shrine was completed here. Martyrs' Shrine: In 1946, after the war, it became a shrine to honor martyrs. Gymnasium: In 1969, the old buildings came down and a city gymnasium went up.

十一號公園：1991 年體育館拆除，地面是公園，地下是停車場。 美術館2館：2019 年 1 月，美術館2館正式開館。

No. 11 Park: In 1991, the site became a park, with a parking lot underground. Art Museum Building 2: In January 2019, Building 2 opened to the public.

坂茂的建築之樹Shigeru Ban's architectural tree

普立茲克獎得主：坂茂在 2014 年獲得普立茲克獎，與石昭永共同設計2館。 錯落的白盒子：白色方盒以不同角度堆疊，沒有唯一的正面。 半戶外空間：方盒之間留下成蔭的半戶外空間，呼應這裡曾是公園。 五角形頂棚：最上方漂浮著巨大的五角形頂棚，向鳳凰木致敬。

A Pritzker Prize laureate: Shigeru Ban won the Pritzker Prize in 2014 and designed Building 2 with Joe Shih. Stacked white boxes: White square boxes are stacked at shifting angles, so there is no single front. Semi-outdoor spaces: Shaded spaces between the boxes recall the site's old life as a park. The pentagonal canopy: A great five-sided canopy floats above it all, in homage to the phoenix tree.

碎形屋頂：重複的幾何圖案像樹葉，讓陽光一格一格灑下。 又詩意又實用：在濕熱的臺南，樹蔭替遊客降溫、為藝術品遮陽。 頂樓的天際線：頂樓平台可同時看到美術館、司法博物館的圓頂和中西區屋瓦。

fractal roof: Its repeating pattern breaks the sunlight into pieces, like leaves. Poetic and practical: In the hot, humid climate, the shade cools visitors and protects the art. The skyline from the top: From the top terrace, you see the courthouse dome and the old town's roofs.

實景照片

Photos on site

2館外觀 The museum outside

坂茂和石昭永共同設計了這座美術館。白色方盒以不同角度錯落堆疊，上方是巨大的屋頂。牆上寫著「臺南市美術館 2館」。

Shigeru Ban and Joe Shih designed this museum. White boxes are stacked at shifting angles under a giant roof.

三角形支柱 Triangle supports

從側面看，斜斜的白色柱子組成一個大三角形，撐起屋頂。白色方盒裡是大大小小的展覽室，方盒頂上種了花草樹木。

From the side, slanted white columns form a big triangle that holds up the roof. The galleries are inside the white boxes, and plants grow on top of them.

三角形裡的三角形 Triangles in triangles

在入口附近抬頭看：屋頂上，大三角形裡有小三角形，一層又一層，這就是「碎形」圖案。它的靈感來自鳳凰花，也替整棟建築遮陽。

Look up near the entrance. The roof has triangles inside triangles. This fractal pattern was inspired by the phoenix flower, and it shades the whole building.

碎形屋頂 Fractal roof

抬頭看：玻璃屋頂上方就是五角形大屋頂，一個個三角形重複排列，形成「碎形」圖案，把強烈的陽光打散成點點光影。

Look up: the fractal roof breaks the strong sunlight into little pieces of light and shade.

建築之樹 An architectural tree

白色鋼柱像樹幹一樣向上分岔，撐起頂樓的玻璃屋頂。抬頭看，就像站在一棵白色大樹下。

These white steel columns branch out like a tree to hold up the glass roof.

大屋頂下 Under the canopy

五角形大屋頂的靈感來自臺南的市花鳳凰花；它幫建築遮陽、降溫。屋頂下是明亮的頂樓空間和玻璃電梯。

The five-sided canopy was inspired by the phoenix flower, and its shade helps keep the building cool.
